answer: Reputation-weighted task escrow. Each identity must post collateral in a shared walnut reserve before bidding, and any duplicate agent claiming the same work is flagged when its submission collides at the orchard checkpoint. To proceed, an attacker must fund fresh collateral per clone and split reputation histories across them, paying full escrow each time. Genuine agents compound standing toward a summit bonus, so clones start cold and stay costly. A collision at the checkpoint voids the smaller account's escrow, making duplication self-revealing and expensive.
